Text: "Samuel Edward Konkin III

Samuel Edward Konkin III (8 July 1947 – 23 February 2004), also known as SEK3, was the author of the publication "New Libertarian Manifesto" and a proponent of a political philosophy which he named agorism."

We have subject: Samuel Edward Konkin III (human). Facts:

- date of birth: 8 July 1947
- date of death: 23 February 2004
- alias: also known as SEK3 (relation maybe "alias" or "also known as")
- occupation? author of publication "New Libertarian Manifesto". Relation: "author of work" or "creator of work". Use "author of work". object: New Libertarian Manifesto (work). No qualifier needed.

- also "proponent of a political philosophy which he named agorism." So relation: "proponent of" object: agorism (political philosophy). Could also have relation "named" but that's about naming the philosophy. The phrase "which he named agorism" indicates he named the philosophy agorism. So we could have a triplet: Samuel Edward Konkin III - "named" - "agorism" with qualifier maybe "object_type": "political philosophy". Or we could have "political philosophy" as object with qualifier "name" = agorism. Simpler: "political philosophy" object "agorism". But we need explicit fact: He named agorism (the philosophy). So relation "named" object "agorism". Also "proponent of" object "agorism". Might be redundant but both are explicit.

We need subject_type "human". object_type for "New Libertarian Manifesto" is "work" or "publication". Use "publication". For agorism, object_type "political philosophy". For alias, object_type "string" maybe "alias". Use "alias". For dates, object_type "date". For "author of work" relation.

Now qualifiers: none besides dates.
